newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK POISTOVNA POSTS JAN-AUG SKK 1.37 BLN GROSS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK POISTOVNA POSTS JAN-AUG SKK 1.37 BLN GROSS.

text.p: Slovakia's largest insurer, state-controlled Slovenska Poistovna a.s., on Tuesday said its January-August pre-tax profit totalled 1.368 billion crowns, up from 1.091 billion in the same period last year.
"Our profit rose by around 277 million crowns in the first eight months of this year compared with the same period last year," Edita Bukovska, Poistovna's General Director, told a news conference.

Revenues totalled roughly 8.555 billion crowns in the January-August period, up from last year's 7.809 billion. Overall expenditures were 7.187 billion crowns, compared with 6.718 billion in the first eight months of 1995.
Bukovska said Poistovna accounted for about 75 percent of the entire Slovak insurance market, on which 20 insurance companies were active.
Back in 1991, as a fully state-owned company, Poistovna controlled 100 percent of the market.
Poistovna, which now claims about one half of the two billion crown basic capital of domestic insurers, currently manages 4.9 million long-term insurance contracts, the company said.
The company is among Slovakia's four largest financial institutions awaiting privatisation.

In January, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said Poistovna, including the two largest commercial banks VUB and IRB, and the largest savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, should be privatised by the end of February.
But the plan was delayed several times before parliament effectively postponed the privatisation until March 1997.
In August Slovak Securities Registry (SCP) figures showed the Kosice-based steelworks VSZ controlled 20.03 percent of Slovenska Poistovna a.s.
Poistovna officials refused to comment on the company's ownership structure. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
